+    def test_subdomain(self, runner):
+        """Test that routes with subdomains show the correct domain."""
+        def create_app():
+            app = Flask(__name__)
+            app.config['SERVER_NAME'] = 'test.local'
+            app.testing = True
+
+            @app.route('/home')
+            def home():
+                pass
+
+            from flask import Blueprint
+            admin_blueprint = Blueprint('admin', __name__)
+
+            @admin_blueprint.route('/home')
+            def admin_home():
+                pass
+
+            app.register_blueprint(admin_blueprint, url_prefix='', subdomain='admin')
+            return app
+
+        cli = FlaskGroup(create_app=create_app)
+        result = runner.invoke(cli, ['routes'])
+        
+        assert result.exit_code == 0
+        # Check that the domain column is present
+        lines = result.output.splitlines()
+        assert 'Domain' in lines[0]
+        # Check that admin.test.local appears in the output
+        assert 'admin.test.local' in result.output
+
+    def test_host(self, runner):
+        """Test that routes with hosts show the correct host."""
+        def create_app():
+            app = Flask(__name__)
+            app.config['SERVER_NAME'] = 'example.com'
+            app.testing = True
+
+            @app.route('/test', host='api.example.com')
+            def api_test():
+                pass
+
+            @app.route('/test')
+            def web_test():
+                pass
+
+            return app
+
+        cli = FlaskGroup(create_app=create_app)
+        result = runner.invoke(cli, ['routes'])
+        
+        assert result.exit_code == 0
+        # Check that the domain/host column is present
+        lines = result.output.splitlines()
+        assert 'Domain' in lines[0]
+        # Check that api.example.com appears in the output
+        assert 'api.example.com' in result.output
